answer.policy_title: Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal CMM-313: Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty
criteria_quotes: The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis.
For individuals with significant medical conditions or comorbidities, the risk/benefit of hip arthroplasty procedures should be clearly documented in the medical record.
Total hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following.

The policy defines total hip replacement as a procedure involving removal of the damaged hip joint and replacement with an artificial prosthesis consisting of a femoral-head component, femoral component, and acetabular component.
answer.appeal_deadline: February 17, 2027. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received within 180 days of August 21, 2026.
answer.submission_route: Call Cigna Customer Service at the telephone number on the back of the member ID card and request an appeal. Cigna's public member guidance says to begin an appeal by calling that number within 180 calendar days of the denial notice and then submit the written appeal and supporting documentation. Cigna's Customer Appeal Request form says to mail the completed form or an appeal letter, the denial notice, and supporting medical records to the address indicated by the ID card: (1) if the card indicates 'GW - Cigna Network': Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188062, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8062; or (2) if the card indicates 'Cigna Network': Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011. The member should use the address printed or otherwise specified for this particular ID card and plan.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The applicable public policy is the CMM-313 policy linked above. The policy states that the specific benefit plan document controls if it conflicts with the policy. Ask Cigna Customer Service and the provider who submitted the prior-authorization request for the complete clinical-review criteria used in reference number POC-892F80BC2E-98290, including the precise CMM-313 total-hip-replacement subsection and any additional plan-specific criteria or rationale. Also request the clinical-reviewer's determination and the records or facts found insufficient. Cigna's member guidance says that the appeal-process information is provided in the written coverage-decision document and may also be obtained by calling Customer Service.

Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V2.0.2025 Definitions CMM.JT.DF.313 v2.0.2025 Hip Arthroplasty an orthopaedic surgical procedure during which the articular surface of the hip joint is replaced, remodeled, or realigned. Hip Replacement a form of arthroplasty that includes the surgical replacement of the hip joint with a prosthesis. Hip Resurfacing Arthroplasty (HRA) (also called metal- on-metal [MoM] hip resurfacing and hemi-resurfacing arthroplasty) a surgical technique that involves the removal of diseased cartilage and bone from the head of the femur, and the replacement of the surface of the femoral head with a metal hemisphere that fits into a metal acetabular cup or into the acetabulum respectively. The technique conserves femoral bone and maintains normal femoral loading and stresses. Because of bone conservation, it may not compromise future total hip replacements. Hip resurfacing arthroplasty has been promoted as an alternative to total hip replacement for younger individuals. Hip resurfacing arthroplasty may be either a partial HRA (i.e., hemi-hip resurfacing, hemi- resurfacing or femoral head resurfacing arthroplasty [FHRA]) or a total HRA. Non-Surgical Management (with regard to the treatment of lower extremity joint pain) any provider-directed non-surgical treatment, which has been demonstrated in the scientific literature as efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of lower extremity joint pain. The types of treatment involved can include, but are not limited to, the following: relative rest/ activity modification; weight loss; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non- prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or, intra- articular injections. Partial Hip Replacement (also called hip hemi- arthroplasty) a surgical technique where only the femoral head (the ball) of the damaged hip joint is replaced. The acetabulum (the socket) is not replaced. Revision of Hip Replacement (Partial or Total) surgical reconstruction or replacement due to failure or complications of previous hip replacement.
